title: Tenant isolation patterns and shipping checklist for private observability
content:
Purpose

This note captures proposed patterns for tenant isolation inside private deployments (VPC or on-prem), pragmatic Terraform module notes for our observability stack, and a concise shipping/checklist + upgrade plan. The focus is on designs that let multiple product tenants or business units share a single private observability installation while preserving: data isolation (logical), query-level access control, cost accounting, and safe upgrade/fallback semantics.

Context and constraints
- Customers want private deployments with one or more tenant boundaries (e.g., BU-A, BU-B) inside a VPC or on-prem cluster.
- Hardware footprint is limited: we expect to colocate monitoring components (prometheus/grafana/OTEL collectors/log shippers) on a constrained set of hosts.
- Compliance often requires separate retention/purge policies per tenant, encryption-at-rest using customer KMS, and audit trails.
- Network topology: private VPCs with restricted egress, some air-gapped installs where S3 is an internal objectstore endpoint.

High-level isolation patterns (tradeoffs)
1) Per-tenant control plane (strong isolation, higher cost)\   - Each tenant gets a dedicated Prometheus instance, TSDB, and Grafana organization.\   - Pros: simple RBAC, separate retention, no cross-tenant leakage. Easy per-tenant upgrades.\   - Cons: disk/CPU multiply by number of tenants; heavy for small tenants.

2) Shared control plane with tenancy labels (efficient, moderate isolation)\   - Single Prometheus (remote_write -> multi-tenant long-term storage) + tenant label applied at the collector/agent.\   - Use relabeling + enforcement so that tenants cannot spoof labels.\   - Pros: resource efficient; simpler metric federation.\   - Cons: requires strict label hygiene and query-level RBAC in Grafana/Query frontend.

3) Hybrid (shared ingest, per-tenant long-term stores)\   - Shared OTEL/Prometheus scrape/agent layer; remote_write splits to per-tenant objectstore buckets or timeseries namespaces (e.g., Thanos/ Cortex / Mimir / Prometheus remote_write + tenant-specific backends).\   - Pros: balance of efficiency and tenant-level retention.\   - Cons: slightly more operational complexity during rollouts.

Recommendation
- Default to pattern (3) Hybrid for most customers. Provide an automated path to convert small tenants to full per-tenant control planes when they exceed resource thresholds.

Terraform module notes (practicalities and variables)
- Module naming: modules/observability/collector, modules/observability/prometheus, modules/observability/remote_write_router, modules/observability/grafana-org, modules/observability/log_shipper
- Key module inputs (example variables we should expose):\   - collector.relabeling_rules: (string) relabel YAML applied at edge; include tenant_id enforcement.\   - collector.default_tenant_label: (string) e.g. tenant_id or account_id.\   - prometheus.shard_count: (int) for sharded installs (default 1).\   - prometheus.pvc_size_gb: (int) dynamically sized by tenant sizing policy.\   - remote_write.router.targets: (list of maps as stringified JSON in Terraform) — internal limitation: for Drive docs we note the variable name only.\   - grafana.orgs: (list) create per-tenant orgs and initial admin users.\   - log_shipper.outputs: s3_bucket, prefix_template, kms_key_arn.
- Opinions to bake into modules:\   - Require explicit tenant label at edge. Collector module should reject start if relabeling_rules would drop tenant label.\   - Provide an optional sidecar mode for collectors: sidecar per-app (minimal CPU) or central collector daemonset (more efficient).\   - Provide IAM/KMS integration variables: kms_key_arn, kms_encrypt_for_tenant.

OTEL Collector patterns and config hygiene
- Two principal deployment modes: sidecar agents (per-app) vs centralized collector cluster (stateful).\- For private infra, prefer a small fleet of regional collectors with ingestion sharding (collector group A/B) and ACLs to only accept from known client certs.
- Enforce tenant identity using mTLS client certs or short-lived tokens issued by local identity service. Collector must inject/verify tenant_id label rather than trusting client-provided label.
- Example relabel flow (collector):\   1) Verify client cert -> map to tenant_id.\   2) Inject tenant_id label into metrics/traces/logs.\   3) Apply tenant-level scrubbing rules (PII redaction plugin).\- OTEL config snippets to include in module: authentication_providers, pipeline stages for metrics/traces/logs, export processors per tenant.

Log shipping and archival
- Use Fluent Bit as the edge shipper for resource efficiency; support Fluentd as optional for complex parsing.\- Ship logs to an internal objectstore (S3-compatible) partitioned by tenant_id/prefix and time window. Example prefix: s3://observability-archive/{tenant_id}/{year}/{month}/{day}/<file>.gz\- Implement server-side encryption with tenant-specific KMS keys when customer asks.\- Implement lifecycle policies: hot (7–14d) -> warm (30–90d) -> cold (archive) -> delete. Terraform should create lifecycle rules per-tenant bucket/prefix.

Prometheus long-term storage and query layer
- Option A: Thanos sidecars + objectstore per-tenant prefixes. Thanos querier with tenant-aware authorization.\- Option B: Cortex/Mimir multi-tenant remote_write ingestion. More scalable for tens of tenants.
- Query isolation: bring a query-frontend that enforces org->tenant mapping. Grafana queries should be proxied through an auth layer that injects tenant filter.

Grafana/Authz
- Provision per-tenant Grafana orgs and dashboards via terraform grafana provider.
- Use Grafana Enterprise or plugin for granular admin roles — default install must lock down org creation.
- Map SSO groups to Grafana roles using SAML/OIDC claims with tenant claim.

Upgrade and rollout plan (prometheus/collectors/grafana/logshipper)
1) Preflight (automated checks)\   - Terraform plan run with dry-run outputs, check module diffs for any changes to bucket policies or IAM.\   - Run a small smoke deploy in staging with the new collector/prometheus image.\   - Verify relabel rules do not drop tenant_id (scripted check).
2) Canary (subset of tenants)\   - Pick low-traffic tenant(s) A + B. Deploy new version of collector and remote_write router.\   - Monitor: scrape success rate, remote_write 200/5xx, queue size, prom scrape durations, error_inject rate.\   - Run query-level smoke tests: simple dashboard queries should return expected series for canary tenants.
3) Ramp (progressive rollout)\   - Roll hosts in waves by availability-zone or node-pool.\   - If persistent failures > 3% of scrapes or remote_write 5xx spike > 1% use automatic rollback.
4) Sweep / Cleanup\   - Reconcile metrics: ensure no gaps, tidy any per-tenant retention changes, run compaction if needed.

Rollback criteria and fast-fail triggers
- High-level: if we detect sustained >2% increase in 5xx remote_write or prometheus scrape failure across >= 2 shards for >10 minutes, trigger rollback.\- Also if query correctness tests for any tenant fail (missing expected series for 3 consecutive checks), rollback.

Operational checklist for cutover (concise)
- Pre-cutover\   - Back up Grafana dashboards (tenant org dumps).\   - Snapshot Prometheus data directories if per-tenant instances.\   - Ensure S3 lifecycle policies are in place for new prefixes.\   - Verify IAM/KMS integration and that keys decrypt on target hosts.
- During cutover\   - Put a short maintenance window for heavy index compactions.\   - Deploy new collector config to canary group.\   - Confirm remote_write target connectivity and S3 write success.\   - Validate logs are arriving at objectstore for canary tenants.\- Post-cutover\   - Run query and alert smoke tests for each tenant org.\   - Re-enable normal alerting thresholds (we set higher tolerance for first 30m).

Playbook snippets (alerts to add)
- OTEL Collector queue depth high: severity=P2 if queue > 80% for >5m.\- Remote_write 5xx spike: severity=P1 if aggregate 5xx rate >1% of traffic for >3m.\- Prometheus scrape latency: severity=P2 if > 2s median for 10m.\- Log shipper S3 write failures: severity=P1 immediate.

Known unresolved questions / tradeoffs to decide
- Tenant access model: do we permit tenant admins to create dashboards? (security vs autonomy)\- How to bill customers for cross-tenant shared costs — taggable metrics vs per-tenant cost aggregation?\- Do we require per-tenant KMS keys for all customers or only for regulated ones?

Next steps (short-term action items)
1) Build Terraform module PR that enforces "tenant label required" check in collector module (owner: Samir) — target: PR by 2025-11-15.\2) Prototype remote_write router that fans to per-tenant prefixes in S3 + Thanos ingest (owner: Lina) — prototype complete by 2025-12-01.\3) Draft Grafana provisioning templates + initial RBAC mapping doc (owner: Ethan) — first pass by 2025-11-20.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic and favors hybrid pattern to manage constrained resources while providing logical isolation. Please call out any security assumptions you disagree with, and any missing terraform variables that you need for compliance audits.
